top.reason: detach() calls emitter.off with a freshly bound function that differs from the one passed to on() in attach(), so the listener is never actually removed and onMessage keeps firing after detach.
Refill and consumption math is consistent with the documented rate-limiting contract; no defect found.
byNewest's comparator returns a boolean instead of a negative/zero/positive number, so Array.sort never receives a negative signal and does not reliably produce newest-first order.
for...in yields string keys, so `index + 1` string-concatenates (e.g. "2"+1 = "21") instead of computing the documented 1-based numeric rank.
The interval callback awaits client.ping() with no catch, so a failed ping never sets healthy=false (contradicting the documented requirement) and produces an unhandled rejection.
lastN slices from visits.length - n - 1, returning n+1 items instead of the documented n most recent visits.
Fire-and-forget delivery with per-item try/catch matches the documented best-effort, non-awaited contract; no defect.
Per-account promise chaining serializes consume() calls in arrival order as documented; no race condition found.
Inclusive range loop and count formula are consistent with documented inclusive semantics.
Sort comparators correctly implement newest-first, alphabetical, and score-descending ordering with no defect shown.
setInterval can fire again before a slow fetch() resolves, so overlapping calls' then callbacks can write this.latest/this.failures out of order, letting an older response overwrite a newer one.
Optional fields are safely handled via optional chaining and nullish coalescing consistent with the Profile type.

top.reason: attach() registers `this.onMessage.bind(this)` but detach() calls off() with a newly created bound function reference, so the listener is never actually removed and forwarding continues after detach().

take() reads BucketState, awaits, then writes tokens-1 derived from that stale read; concurrent take() calls for the same clientId (normal for a per-request rate limiter) both read the same state and both succeed, letting requests exceed capacity.

sort comparator returns a boolean instead of a numeric difference, so Array.prototype.sort (which expects negative/0/positive) does not reliably order posts by publishedAt descending, producing incorrectly ordered feed output.
for...in yields string keys, so `rank: index + 1` string-concatenates (e.g. "9"+1 => "91") instead of computing a numeric rank as documented.

The setInterval async callback awaits client.ping() with no catch, so a failed ping neither calls markUnhealthy() (contradicting the documented requirement) nor is the rejection handled, becoming an unhandled rejection.
lastN slices from visits.length - n - 1 instead of visits.length - n, returning n+1 items instead of the documented n most recent visits.
Fire-and-forget delivery with internal try/catch logging matches the documented best-effort, non-awaited contract; no defect.
Per-account queue chains promises and guards deletion with an identity check, so serialization and cleanup are correct.
Both helpers treat the range as inclusive on both ends consistently with the documented contract.
Comparators match their documented ordering (newest first, alphabetical, highest score first).
setInterval can fire again before a prior fetch() promise resolves, so overlapping calls can resolve out of order and an older fetch's result can overwrite latest/failures set by a newer one.
Optional chaining and nullish coalescing correctly handle absent address and theme; no defect found.
